entries.body:
# Predator's Pursuit

## Overview
Predator's Pursuit is the moment a Ranger's hunt becomes something more than skill alone. By calling upon ancient primal magic, the Ranger forms a mystical bond with a single quarry, allowing the wilderness itself to reveal subtle traces of the creature's passage. What once required careful observation now seems to appear naturally before the hunter's eyes.

The marked quarry becomes easier to follow wherever it travels. Faint spectral signs illuminate its trail, while the Ranger instinctively senses the direction of the hunt. Although the quarry may flee, hide, or attempt to erase its tracks, the wilderness quietly guides the Ranger towards its inevitable destination.

---

## Rank 1
### Description

Predator's Pursuit is the moment a Ranger's hunt becomes something more than skill alone. By calling upon ancient primal magic, the Ranger forms a mystical bond with a single quarry, allowing the wilderness itself to reveal subtle traces of the creature's passage. What once required careful observation now seems to appear naturally before the hunter's eyes.

The marked quarry becomes easier to follow wherever it travels. Faint spectral signs illuminate its trail, while the Ranger instinctively senses the direction of the hunt. Although the quarry may flee, hide, or attempt to erase its tracks, the wilderness quietly guides the Ranger towards its inevitable destination.

---

### Effects

- **Cost:** 50 MP.
- Choose one creature you can see to become your **Quarry**.
- The mark lasts for **1 hour**, or until:
  - The Quarry dies.
  - The Quarry becomes unconscious.
  - You willingly end the effect.
  - You mark another creature.

#### Hunter's Mark Synergy

- If a creature is already affected by your **Hunter's Mark**, it automatically becomes your **Quarry** when Predator's Pursuit is activated.
- If **Hunter's Mark** is transferred to another creature, **Predator's Pursuit** immediately transfers to the same creature without requiring another Mana Cost or action.
- If no creature is affected by Hunter's Mark, choose a Quarry normally.

#### While your Quarry is marked

- The Quarry is outlined by a **faint spectral glow** visible only to you while it remains within your line of sight.
- Footprints, blood trails, broken vegetation, disturbed earth, and other signs left by the Quarry emit a **soft magical glow** visible only to you.
- You always know the **general direction** of your Quarry while it remains within **1 kilometre** and on the same plane of existence.
- Gain **Advantage** on **Survival** checks made to track your Quarry.
- While **Hidden** or benefiting from **Cover**, gain a **+2 bonus to attack rolls** against your marked Quarry.
- Your marked Quarry gains **no benefit from Half Cover** against your ranged attacks.
- Non-magical attempts to conceal or erase the Quarry's trail have **Disadvantage** against your tracking attempts.

#### Limitations

- The spectral outline does not reveal the Quarry through solid objects or magical barriers.
- The bond reveals only the Quarry's **general direction**, not its exact location or distance.
- Magical concealment, teleportation, or planar travel may suppress the connection, at the GM's discretion.
- Only one creature may be your Quarry at a time.

---

### Lore

The oldest Ranger Lodges teach that every hunt leaves an echo within the wilderness. Those who prove themselves worthy may one day learn to see these echoes, following trails that ordinary eyes could never perceive. To outsiders, Predator's Pursuit appears to be remarkable tracking. Rangers know the truth—it is the wilderness choosing to guide the hunter.

Legends tell of Huntmasters pursuing monsters across entire kingdoms, guided only by glowing footprints and an unwavering instinct that never led them astray. Once the wilderness accepts a Ranger's quarry, few creatures escape the hunt for long.

---

> *"The quarry may hide from my eyes, but it cannot hide from the wilderness."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood, First Huntmaster of the Emerald Lodge**

## Rank 2
### Description

The Ranger's bond with their quarry grows stronger, allowing the primal magic of the wilderness to reveal far more than simple tracks. Every footprint, broken branch, and drop of blood shines brighter, while even older trails become easier to follow. The hunt begins to feel less like a search and more like an invisible thread connecting hunter and prey.

Experienced Rangers speak of reaching a point where the wilderness itself refuses to let their quarry disappear. Whether travelling through dense forests, rocky mountains, or open plains, subtle signs continually guide the Ranger forward. The prey may attempt to hide its trail, but nature remembers every step it has taken.

---

### Effects

- **Cost:** 60 MP.
- Choose one creature you can see to become your **Quarry**.
- The mark lasts for **2 hours**, or until:
  - The Quarry dies.
  - The Quarry becomes unconscious.
  - You willingly end the effect.
  - You mark another creature.

#### Hunter's Mark Synergy

- If a creature is already affected by your **Hunter's Mark**, it automatically becomes your **Quarry**.
- If **Hunter's Mark** is transferred to another creature, **Predator's Pursuit** immediately transfers as well without requiring another Mana Cost or action.
- If no creature is affected by Hunter's Mark, choose a Quarry normally.

#### While your Quarry is marked

- The Quarry is surrounded by a **clear spectral outline** visible only to you while within your line of sight.
- Tracks, blood trails, disturbed vegetation, broken branches, scents, and other signs left by the Quarry emit a brighter magical glow visible only to you.
- You always know the **general direction** of your Quarry while it remains within **5 kilometres** and on the same plane of existence.
- Gain **Advantage** on **Survival** and **Perception** checks made to locate or track your Quarry.
- While **Hidden** or benefiting from **Cover**, gain a **+3 bonus to attack rolls** against your marked Quarry.
- Your marked Quarry gains **no benefit from Half Cover or Three-Quarters Cover** against your ranged attacks.
- Non-magical attempts to conceal, erase, or disguise the Quarry's trail automatically fail against your tracking attempts.

#### Limitations

- The spectral outline does not reveal the Quarry through solid objects or magical barriers.
- The bond reveals only the Quarry's general direction, not its exact location or distance.
- Powerful magical concealment, teleportation, or planar travel may suppress the connection at the GM's discretion.
- Only one creature may be your Quarry at a time.

---

### Lore

Those who master the second rank of Predator's Pursuit begin to understand that the wilderness does more than reveal tracks—it remembers them. Every trail left by the quarry becomes another page in a story only the Ranger can read, guiding them with unwavering certainty through forests, mountains, and forgotten ruins alike.

Within the Ranger Lodges, hunters capable of maintaining this bond are rarely assigned ordinary prey. They are entrusted with tracking dangerous monsters, escaped criminals, and creatures that others have long since declared impossible to find.

---

> *"A trail may vanish beneath the wind, but the wilderness never forgets who walked upon it."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 3
### Description

The bond between the Ranger and their Quarry has become deeply intertwined with the primal magic of the wilderness. The marked creature can no longer easily disappear, as nature itself continuously reveals subtle signs of its passage. Even when tracks are scarce, the Ranger's instincts are guided by an unseen force that steadily draws them closer to their prey.

Veteran Rangers describe this connection as becoming one with the hunt. Every footprint shines with spectral light, every broken branch tells a story, and even the faintest disturbance in the environment becomes impossible to overlook. Once marked, the Quarry soon learns that escape is far more difficult than survival.

---

### Effects

- **Cost:** 70 MP.
- Choose one creature you can see to become your **Quarry**.
- The mark lasts for **4 hours**, or until:
  - The Quarry dies.
  - The Quarry becomes unconscious.
  - You willingly end the effect.
  - You mark another creature.

#### Hunter's Mark Synergy

- If a creature is already affected by your **Hunter's Mark**, it automatically becomes your **Quarry**.
- If **Hunter's Mark** is transferred to another creature, **Predator's Pursuit** immediately transfers to that creature without requiring another Mana Cost or action.
- If no creature is affected by **Hunter's Mark**, choose a Quarry normally.

#### While your Quarry is marked

- The Quarry is surrounded by a **bright spectral outline** visible only to you while it remains within your line of sight.
- Tracks, blood, scents, broken vegetation, and all signs of the Quarry's passage emit a vivid magical glow visible only to you.
- You always know the **general direction** of your Quarry while it remains within **20 kilometres** and on the same plane of existence.
- Gain **Advantage** on **Survival**, **Perception**, and **Investigation** checks made to locate or pursue your Quarry.
- While **Hidden** or benefiting from **Cover**, gain a **+4 bonus to attack rolls** against your marked Quarry.
- Your marked Quarry gains **no benefit from any non-magical cover** against your ranged attacks.
- **Non-magical disguises, false trails, or attempts to conceal the Quarry's tracks automatically fail** against your tracking attempts.

#### Limitations

- The spectral outline does not reveal the Quarry through solid objects or magical barriers.
- The bond reveals only the Quarry's general direction, not its exact location or distance.
- Powerful magical concealment, teleportation, or planar travel may suppress the connection at the GM's discretion.
- Only one creature may be your Quarry at a time.

---

### Lore

Rangers who achieve the third rank of Predator's Pursuit are no longer simply following tracks—they are following the will of the wilderness itself. Their connection with nature has grown so strong that the land seems eager to reveal the movements of the chosen Quarry. Every broken twig, displaced stone, and drop of blood becomes another guide along the hunt.

Within the Ranger Lodges, these hunters are often tasked with pursuing creatures that others consider impossible to track. Many legends tell of Rangers following a single Quarry across entire mountain ranges, through dense forests and forgotten ruins, never once losing the trail until the hunt reached its inevitable end.

---

> *"You can hide your footprints from men. You cannot hide them from the wilderness."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 4
### Description

The Ranger's connection to the wilderness has become extraordinarily powerful. Once a Quarry has been chosen, the natural world actively reveals its movements, making escape almost impossible. The bond transcends simple tracking, allowing the Ranger to instinctively understand the state of their prey even across vast distances.

Every step the Quarry takes leaves behind an echo only the Ranger can perceive. Ancient trees, flowing rivers, shifting winds, and the creatures of the wild all seem to quietly guide the hunter toward their destination. Though the Quarry may flee through forests, mountains, or deserts, the wilderness refuses to let it disappear completely.

Among the Ranger Lodges, those who master this rank are known as **Wildseekers**, hunters entrusted with tracking the most dangerous beasts and elusive foes across entire regions of Asteria.

---

### Effects

- **Cost:** 80 MP.
- Choose one creature you can see to become your **Quarry**.
- The mark lasts for **8 hours**, or until:
  - The Quarry dies.
  - The Quarry becomes unconscious.
  - You willingly end the effect.
  - You mark another creature.

#### Hunter's Mark Synergy

- If a creature is already affected by your **Hunter's Mark**, it automatically becomes your **Quarry**.
- If **Hunter's Mark** is transferred to another creature, **Predator's Pursuit** immediately transfers to that creature without requiring another Mana Cost or action.
- If no creature is affected by **Hunter's Mark**, choose a Quarry normally.

#### While your Quarry is marked

- The Quarry is surrounded by a **brilliant spectral outline** visible only to you while it remains within your line of sight.
- Tracks, blood trails, scents, disturbed vegetation, broken objects, and every other sign of the Quarry's passage emit a vivid magical glow visible only to you.
- You always know the **general direction** of your Quarry while it remains within **50 kilometres** and on the same plane of existence.
- You instinctively know whether your Quarry is **moving**, **stationary**, or **incapacitated**.
- Gain **Advantage** on **Survival**, **Perception**, and **Investigation** checks made to locate or pursue your Quarry.
- While **Hidden** or benefiting from **Cover**, gain a **+5 bonus to attack rolls** against your marked Quarry.
- Your marked Quarry gains **no benefit from non-magical cover or concealment** against your ranged attacks.
- Non-magical disguises, false trails, and attempts to conceal the Quarry's presence automatically fail against your tracking attempts.

#### Limitations

- The spectral outline does not reveal the Quarry through solid objects or magical barriers.
- The bond reveals only the Quarry's general direction and current state, not its exact location or distance.
- Powerful magical concealment, teleportation, or planar travel may suppress the connection at the GM's discretion.
- Only one creature may be your Quarry at a time.

---

### Lore

The fourth rank of Predator's Pursuit is regarded as one of the greatest honours within the Ranger Lodges. Wildseekers are often dispatched on missions that span entire kingdoms, pursuing monsters, warlords, and fugitives who have escaped every other hunter. Their success comes not from unmatched speed, but from an unwavering connection with the wilderness itself.

Legends tell of Rangers who pursued Dragons across mountain ranges and tracked ancient horrors through forgotten forests without ever losing the trail. To them, the wilderness is no longer simply a place to survive—it has become a trusted companion in the hunt.

---

> *"A quarry may outrun the hunter, but it can never outrun the wilderness."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 5
### Description

The Ranger has become the ultimate hunter, forming a bond with their Quarry so profound that the wilderness itself refuses to let the creature vanish. Mountains, forests, deserts, rivers, and plains all become silent allies, revealing fragments of the Quarry's journey through subtle whispers only the Ranger can perceive.

No longer limited to following physical tracks, the Ranger senses the hunt itself. Every movement of the Quarry leaves an echo within the natural world, guiding the Ranger with unwavering certainty. Escape is still possible, but only through extraordinary means. Once marked, the Quarry carries the attention of both the Ranger and the wilderness until the hunt reaches its conclusion.

Among the Ranger Lodges, this mastery is known as **The Eternal Hunt**, a title reserved for those whose prey is said to have nowhere left to hide.

---

### Effects

- **Cost:** 90 MP.
- Choose one creature you can see to become your **Quarry**.
- The mark lasts for **24 hours**, or until:
  - The Quarry dies.
  - The Quarry becomes unconscious.
  - You willingly end the effect.
  - You mark another creature.

#### Hunter's Mark Synergy

- If a creature is already affected by your **Hunter's Mark**, it automatically becomes your **Quarry**.
- If **Hunter's Mark** is transferred to another creature, **Predator's Pursuit** immediately transfers to that creature without requiring another Mana Cost or action.
- If no creature is affected by **Hunter's Mark**, choose a Quarry normally.

#### While your Quarry is marked

- The Quarry is surrounded by a **brilliant primal aura** visible only to you whenever it is within your line of sight.
- Footprints, blood trails, disturbed vegetation, broken terrain, scents, and every other trace left by the Quarry emit a radiant magical glow visible only to you.
- You always know the **general direction** of your Quarry anywhere on the **same continent**, provided it remains on the same plane of existence.
- You instinctively know whether your Quarry is:
  - Moving.
  - Stationary.
  - Resting.
  - In combat.
  - Seriously wounded.
- Gain **Advantage** on **Survival**, **Perception**, and **Investigation** checks related to locating or pursuing your Quarry.
- While **Hidden** or benefiting from **Cover**, gain a **+6 bonus to attack rolls** against your marked Quarry.
- Your marked Quarry gains **no benefit from cover or non-magical concealment** against your ranged attacks.
- Non-magical disguises, false trails, hidden tracks, and attempts to conceal the Quarry's presence automatically fail against your tracking attempts.

#### Limitations

- The primal aura does not reveal the Quarry through solid objects or magical barriers.
- The bond reveals only the Quarry's general direction and condition, never its exact location.
- Powerful magical concealment, teleportation, planar travel, or divine intervention may suppress the connection at the GM's discretion.
- Only one creature may be your Quarry at a time.

---

### Lore

Only a handful of Rangers throughout history have ever mastered Predator's Pursuit to this extent. Their names are remembered in legend, not because their prey was weak, but because nothing they pursued ever truly escaped. Kings sought their aid to track assassins, guilds relied upon them to hunt monsters, and entire armies respected the terrifying certainty with which these Rangers followed their chosen Quarry.

The Ranger Lodges teach that this technique is not about domination, but harmony. By earning the trust of the wilderness over a lifetime of respect and perseverance, the Ranger becomes part of nature's endless cycle. Every trail, every breeze, and every whispering tree serves the hunt until hunter and Quarry are finally brought together once more.

---

> *"The hunt does not end when my Quarry disappears. It ends when the wilderness decides our paths shall cross again."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood, First Huntmaster of the Emerald Lodge**

## Prerequisites
None

entries.body:
# Whirlwind Evasion

## Overview
A Ranger's greatest defence is not armour, but movement. Through years of surviving against faster, larger, and deadlier predators, Rangers learn to react instinctively the moment danger presents itself. A single step, pivot, or roll is often enough to turn a fatal strike into a harmless miss.

Whirlwind Evasion channels this philosophy into a disciplined combat technique. Rather than standing firm, the Ranger moves like the wind itself, flowing around attacks with graceful precision before slipping into a more advantageous position. Every movement is deliberate, preserving momentum while creating opportunities to continue the hunt.

---

## Rank 1
### Description

A Ranger's greatest defence is not armour, but movement. Through years of surviving against faster, larger, and deadlier predators, Rangers learn to react instinctively the moment danger presents itself. A single step, pivot, or roll is often enough to turn a fatal strike into a harmless miss.

Whirlwind Evasion channels this philosophy into a disciplined combat technique. Rather than standing firm, the Ranger moves like the wind itself, flowing around attacks with graceful precision before slipping into a more advantageous position. Every movement is deliberate, preserving momentum while creating opportunities to continue the hunt.

---

### Effects

- **Cost:** 40 SP.
- Activate this ability as a **Reaction** when you are targeted by an attack.
- Until the **start of your next turn**, gain the following benefits:
  - **+2 AC.**
  - **+2** to **Dexterity Saving Throws**.
  - Immediately move **up to 3 metres** without spending Movement.
  - This movement must end on solid ground.
  - The creature whose attack triggered this ability **cannot make an Opportunity Attack** against you during this movement.
- This movement does not interrupt your current turn or prevent you from taking actions on your next turn.

#### Limitations

- May only be activated **once per round**.
- Cannot move through creatures or solid objects.
- Does not negate attacks that have already hit before this ability is activated.

---

### Lore

Among the Ranger Lodges, students are taught to study the movements of nature's greatest hunters. Wolves circle before striking, hawks ride unseen currents of air, and great cats avoid danger through perfect timing rather than brute strength. Rangers learn that survival belongs to those who keep moving.

Veteran Rangers appear almost impossible to corner in battle. Enemies often believe they have trapped their prey, only to find the Ranger already standing elsewhere before the attack can land. To them, every dodge is simply another step in the hunt.

---

> *"Stand still and become the target. Move with the wind, and become the hunter once more."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 2
### Description

The Ranger's movements become increasingly fluid, allowing them to weave through combat with remarkable precision. Every attack is met with an instinctive sidestep, every swing anticipated moments before it lands. What once required conscious effort has become second nature, allowing the Ranger to maintain complete awareness while repositioning with incredible speed.

At this level, Whirlwind Evasion is more than a defensive technique—it is a seamless transition between defence and opportunity. The Ranger avoids danger without losing momentum, always seeking the next advantageous position from which to continue the hunt.

---

### Effects

- **Cost:** 50 SP.
- Activate this ability as a **Reaction** when you are targeted by an attack.
- Until the **start of your next turn**, gain the following benefits:
  - **+3 AC.**
  - **+3** to **Dexterity Saving Throws**.
  - Immediately move **up to 4 metres** without spending Movement.
  - This movement must end on solid ground.
  - The creature whose attack triggered this ability **cannot make an Opportunity Attack** against you during this movement.
- This movement does not interrupt your current turn or prevent you from taking actions on your next turn.

#### Limitations

- May only be activated **once per round**.
- Cannot move through creatures or solid objects.
- Does not negate attacks that have already hit before this ability is activated.

---

### Lore

Experienced Rangers understand that survival is measured not by the number of attacks endured, but by the number successfully avoided. Every hunt, every duel, and every close encounter refines their instincts until movement becomes almost effortless. Opponents often find themselves striking only empty air as the Ranger has already slipped beyond reach.

Within the Ranger Lodges, mastering the second rank of Whirlwind Evasion is considered proof that a hunter has begun to move with the rhythm of the battlefield itself. Like the wind through the trees, their path is difficult to predict and even harder to stop.

---

> *"The quickest step is not the one taken first—it is the one your enemy never sees."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 3
### Description

The Ranger has mastered the ability to move with complete harmony amidst the chaos of battle. Every attack is met with fluid, instinctive motion, allowing the Ranger to evade danger while maintaining perfect control over their footing and surroundings. Rather than reacting after an attack begins, the Ranger seems to anticipate it moments before it is unleashed.

As the technique matures, terrain itself becomes less of an obstacle. Dense undergrowth, loose rocks, fallen trees, and uneven ground fail to interrupt the Ranger's movement, allowing them to reposition with graceful precision even in the harshest environments.

---

### Effects

- **Cost:** 60 SP.
- Activate this ability as a **Reaction** when you are targeted by an attack.
- Until the **start of your next turn**, gain the following benefits:
  - **+4 AC.**
  - **+4** to **Dexterity Saving Throws**.
  - Immediately move **up to 5 metres** without spending Movement.
  - Ignore **non-magical difficult terrain** during this movement.
  - This movement must end on solid ground.
  - The creature whose attack triggered this ability **cannot make an Opportunity Attack** against you during this movement.
- This movement does not interrupt your current turn or prevent you from taking actions on your next turn.

#### Limitations

- May only be activated **once per round**.
- Cannot move through creatures or solid objects.
- Does not negate attacks that have already hit before this ability is activated.

---

### Lore

To seasoned Rangers, movement is as important as marksmanship. Every root, stone, and branch becomes part of the battlefield rather than an obstacle upon it. Those who master the third rank of Whirlwind Evasion move with such effortless precision that even experienced warriors struggle to predict where they will be from one heartbeat to the next.

Within the Ranger Lodges, this technique is often demonstrated in dense forests, where apprentices must weave between trees and natural hazards while avoiding attacks from multiple instructors. Only those who learn to trust both their instincts and the wilderness earn the right to progress further.

---

> *"The forest never asks permission before it moves. Neither should a Ranger."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 4
### Description

The Ranger has become almost untouchable in combat, weaving through the battlefield with speed and precision that few can match. Every dodge flows seamlessly into the next, allowing the Ranger to reposition before opponents can adapt. Their movements resemble the wind itself—swift, unpredictable, and impossible to restrain.

At this level, Whirlwind Evasion is no longer simply a defensive manoeuvre. The Ranger has learned to exploit even the smallest opening, slipping between enemies and escaping situations that would trap almost any other combatant. To those watching from afar, it appears as though the Ranger simply vanishes before reappearing elsewhere on the battlefield.

---

### Effects

- **Cost:** 70 SP.
- Activate this ability as a **Reaction** when you are targeted by an attack.
- Until the **start of your next turn**, gain the following benefits:
  - **+5 AC.**
  - **+5** to **Dexterity Saving Throws**.
  - Immediately move **up to 6 metres** without spending Movement.
  - Ignore **non-magical difficult terrain** during this movement.
  - You may move through the spaces of **Medium or smaller creatures**, treating them as difficult terrain. You must end your movement in an unoccupied space.
  - The creature whose attack triggered this ability **cannot make an Opportunity Attack** against you during this movement.
- This movement does not interrupt your current turn or prevent you from taking actions on your next turn.

#### Limitations

- May only be activated **once per round**.
- Cannot move through solid objects or impassable terrain.
- Does not negate attacks that have already hit before this ability is activated.

---

### Lore

Only veteran Rangers achieve the fourth rank of Whirlwind Evasion. Their movements have become so refined that even experienced duelists struggle to follow them. Every dodge is calculated, every step deliberate, allowing the Ranger to escape seemingly impossible situations without sacrificing control of the battlefield.

Within the Ranger Lodges, masters often describe this technique as "becoming the wind." Like a powerful gust slipping effortlessly through the trees, the Ranger cannot be pinned down for long. Their enemies soon discover that every failed strike leaves them more vulnerable than the Ranger they sought to corner.

---

> *"You cannot trap the wind. You can only wonder where it will strike next."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 5
### Description

The Ranger has perfected Whirlwind Evasion, becoming the embodiment of speed, agility, and instinct. Their movements are so fluid that opponents often struggle to comprehend where the Ranger has gone, striking only the space they once occupied. Every dodge flows naturally into another, allowing the Ranger to evade danger while positioning themselves for the next decisive attack.

To the greatest Huntmasters, movement is no longer a reaction—it is prediction. Every shift in an opponent's stance, every tightening of a grip, and every glance betrays an incoming attack before it is unleashed. Guided by instinct and experience, the Ranger slips effortlessly through the battlefield, impossible to corner and incredibly difficult to strike.

---

### Effects

- **Cost:** 80 SP.
- Activate this ability as a **Reaction** when you are targeted by an attack.
- Until the **start of your next turn**, gain the following benefits:
  - **+6 AC.**
  - **+6** to **Dexterity Saving Throws**.
  - Immediately move **up to 9 metres** without spending Movement.
  - Ignore **all non-magical difficult terrain** during this movement.
  - You may move through the spaces of creatures **Large or smaller**, treating them as difficult terrain. You must end your movement in an unoccupied space.
  - The creature whose attack triggered this ability **cannot make an Opportunity Attack** against you during this movement.
- **If the triggering attack misses**, you may immediately make **one ranged weapon attack** against that creature as part of the same Reaction.
- This movement does not interrupt your current turn or prevent you from taking actions on your next turn.

#### Limitations

- May only be activated **once per round**.
- Cannot move through solid objects or impassable terrain.
- The bonus attack may only target the creature whose attack triggered Whirlwind Evasion.
- The bonus attack cannot benefit from **Multi Shot** or similar abilities that grant additional attacks.

---

### Lore

Only the legendary Huntmasters of Asteria ever achieve the fifth rank of Whirlwind Evasion. Their movements have become so refined that stories often exaggerate them into myth, claiming they vanish into the wind itself before reappearing with bow already drawn. While the truth is less magical, their mastery of timing and movement is no less extraordinary.

Within the Ranger Lodges, this technique is regarded as the ultimate expression of survival. The greatest hunters know that victory is not earned by enduring every blow, but by ensuring the enemy never lands one. Those who witness a master Ranger employ Whirlwind Evasion often realise too late that the hunt has already turned against them.

---

> *"The deadliest Ranger is not the one who stands their ground. It is the one you can never catch."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood, First Huntmaster of the Emerald Lodge**

None

entries.body:
# Phantom Ranger

## Overview
Among the oldest Ranger Lodges, there are whispered tales of hunters who could vanish in the middle of battle without casting a spell of invisibility. These legendary warriors learned to briefly step into the Spirit of the Wild, allowing the physical world to pass around them before emerging from an entirely unexpected position.

Phantom Ranger is the beginning of that mastery. By channelling primal magic, the Ranger momentarily shifts into a spectral state, slipping free from close-quarters combat before melting back into the surrounding wilderness. This brief transition creates the perfect opportunity to disappear from an enemy's sight and continue the hunt from the shadows.

---

## Rank 1
### Description

Among the oldest Ranger Lodges, there are whispered tales of hunters who could vanish in the middle of battle without casting a spell of invisibility. These legendary warriors learned to briefly step into the Spirit of the Wild, allowing the physical world to pass around them before emerging from an entirely unexpected position.

Phantom Ranger is the beginning of that mastery. By channelling primal magic, the Ranger momentarily shifts into a spectral state, slipping free from close-quarters combat before melting back into the surrounding wilderness. This brief transition creates the perfect opportunity to disappear from an enemy's sight and continue the hunt from the shadows.

---

### Effects

- **Cost:** 80 MP.
- **Duration:** 1 Minute.
- **Uses:** 2 uses per **Short Rest**.

While Phantom Ranger is active:

- **Once per turn**, after leaving a creature's melee reach, you may activate **Phantom Step**.
- During **Phantom Step**:
  - Move up to **6 metres**.
  - **Non-magical melee attacks**, including **Opportunity Attacks**, pass harmlessly through your spectral form.
  - **Magical melee attacks, spells, magical ranged attacks, and magical area effects** affect you normally.
  - You may move through creatures, but **not** through walls, solid objects, terrain, or magical barriers.
- At the end of the movement, you may immediately attempt a **Stealth** check to **Hide**, even while combat is ongoing.
- If successful, you become **Hidden** and gain the normal benefits of attacking from Hidden.
- If you know the **Camouflage** talent, you may immediately enter **Camouflage** after successfully becoming Hidden, ignoring Camouflage's normal requirement of being out of combat.

#### Limitations

- You are **not invisible** while using Phantom Step.
- Phantom Step must begin by **leaving a creature's melee reach**.
- You must end the movement in an **unoccupied space**.
- Creatures with magical detection or similar abilities can still detect you normally.

---

### Lore

Only a handful of Rangers ever awaken the gift of Phantom Ranger. Those who do speak of hearing the wilderness itself calling them between heartbeats, allowing them to step beyond the reach of ordinary steel before returning to continue the hunt. To their enemies, it appears as though the Ranger simply dissolves into mist before reappearing elsewhere on the battlefield.

Within the Ranger Lodges, Phantom Rangers are considered living legends. They do not rely on invisibility or illusion, but on a fleeting harmony with the primal spirits of the wild. Every disappearance is deliberate, every reappearance perfectly timed, reminding their quarry that the most dangerous hunter is the one who is never where you expect them to be.

---

> *"The prey watches where I stood. The wise hunter has already moved."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood, First Phantom Ranger**

## Rank 2
### Description

The Ranger's connection to the Spirit of the Wild grows stronger, allowing them to remain between the physical and spiritual worlds for longer periods. Each Phantom Step becomes more fluid, enabling the Ranger to disappear from one engagement before silently emerging somewhere entirely unexpected. Enemies often struggle to determine whether the Ranger truly vanished or simply moved faster than the eye could follow.

Experienced Phantom Rangers no longer rely solely on the terrain to conceal them. Their spectral movements disrupt an opponent's focus, creating brief moments of uncertainty that can be exploited to regain the advantage. Every successful disappearance allows the Ranger to dictate the flow of battle rather than react to it.

---

### Effects

- **Cost:** 90 MP.
- **Duration:** 2 Minutes.
- **Uses:** 2 uses per **Short Rest**.

While Phantom Ranger is active:

- **Once per turn**, after leaving a creature's melee reach, you may activate **Phantom Step**.
- During **Phantom Step**:
  - Move up to **9 metres**.
  - **Non-magical melee attacks**, including **Opportunity Attacks**, pass harmlessly through your spectral form.
  - **Magical melee attacks, spells, magical ranged attacks, and magical area effects** affect you normally.
  - You may move through creatures, but **not** through walls, solid objects, terrain, or magical barriers.
- At the end of the movement, immediately attempt a **Stealth** check to **Hide**, even while combat is ongoing.
- If successful, you become **Hidden** and gain the normal benefits of attacking from Hidden.
- If you possess the **Camouflage** talent, you may immediately enter **Camouflage** after successfully becoming Hidden, ignoring its normal requirement of being out of combat.
- Gain a **+2 bonus** to your Stealth check made as part of Phantom Step.

#### Limitations

- You are **not invisible** while using Phantom Step.
- Phantom Step must begin by **leaving a creature's melee reach**.
- You must end the movement in an **unoccupied space**.
- Creatures with magical detection or similar abilities can still detect you normally.

---

### Lore

To witness a Rank II Phantom Ranger is to question whether they ever occupied the space at all. Hunters trained in this ancient technique weave between the physical and spiritual worlds with remarkable grace, leaving behind only fleeting echoes of their presence. Their movements are so seamless that many foes instinctively strike at where the Ranger once stood, only to find empty air.

Within the Ranger Lodges, these hunters are often entrusted with missions requiring infiltration, reconnaissance, and the elimination of dangerous targets deep behind enemy lines. Their greatest weapon is not their bow or blade, but the uncertainty they leave in the minds of those who seek them.

---

> *"A phantom is not unseen because it is invisible. It is unseen because you looked in the wrong place."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 3
### Description

The Ranger's mastery of Phantom Ranger has deepened, allowing them to walk the boundary between the physical world and the Spirit of the Wild with remarkable ease. Each Phantom Step becomes longer, quieter, and more difficult to follow, leaving enemies striking at fading afterimages while the true hunter has already repositioned.

Veteran Phantom Rangers no longer rely solely on the environment to disappear. Their movements are so fluid that they seem to dissolve into the battlefield itself, using every shadow, tree, and obstacle to remain unseen. To their quarry, the Ranger becomes an ever-present threat that appears only long enough to strike before vanishing once again.

---

### Effects

- **Cost:** 100 MP.
- **Duration:** 3 Minutes.
- **Uses:** 2 uses per **Short Rest**.

While Phantom Ranger is active:

- **Once per turn**, after leaving a creature's melee reach, you may activate **Phantom Step**.
- During **Phantom Step**:
  - Move up to **12 metres**.
  - **Non-magical melee attacks**, including **Opportunity Attacks**, pass harmlessly through your spectral form.
  - **Magical melee attacks, spells, magical ranged attacks, and magical area effects** affect you normally.
  - You may move through creatures of **Large size or smaller**, but not through walls, solid objects, terrain, or magical barriers.
- At the end of the movement, immediately attempt a **Stealth** check to **Hide**, even while combat is ongoing.
- Gain a **+4 bonus** to the Stealth check made as part of Phantom Step.

- If you possess the **Camouflage** talent, you may immediately enter **Camouflage** after successfully becoming Hidden, ignoring its normal requirement of being out of combat.

#### Limitations

- Phantom Step must begin by **leaving a creature's melee reach**.
- You must end the movement in an **unoccupied space**.
- Creatures with magical detection or similar abilities can still detect you normally.

---

### Lore

To master the third rank of Phantom Ranger is to become a living ghost upon the battlefield. The wilderness no longer simply conceals the Ranger—it seems to embrace them, allowing them to drift through the chaos of combat with uncanny precision before emerging where no enemy expected.

Within the Ranger Lodges, these hunters are entrusted with the most dangerous assignments, from infiltrating enemy strongholds to pursuing legendary beasts through dense forests and forgotten ruins. Those who survive an encounter with a Phantom Ranger often struggle to describe what happened, remembering only fleeting glimpses of a spectral figure that seemed to vanish with every heartbeat.

---

> *"The wisest prey never fears the arrow. It fears the silence before it is loosed."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 4
### Description

The Ranger has become a true spectre of the battlefield, able to disappear and reappear with unnerving precision. Their mastery of Phantom Step allows them to break an opponent's focus, reposition through the chaos of combat, and strike before their quarry can recover. To those who face them, every shadow becomes a potential threat.

At this stage, Phantom Ranger is no longer simply an escape technique—it becomes an offensive tool. The Ranger uses every disappearance to create the perfect angle of attack, re-emerging from concealment with devastating precision before once again melting back into the wilderness.

---

### Effects

- **Cost:** 110 MP.
- **Duration:** 4 Minutes.
- **Uses:** 2 uses per **Short Rest**.

While Phantom Ranger is active:

- **Once per turn**, after leaving a creature's melee reach, you may activate **Phantom Step**.
- During **Phantom Step**:
  - Move up to **15 metres**.
  - **Non-magical melee attacks**, including **Opportunity Attacks**, pass harmlessly through your spectral form.
  - **Magical melee attacks, spells, magical ranged attacks, and magical area effects** affect you normally.
  - You may move through creatures of **Large size or smaller**, but not through walls, solid objects, terrain, or magical barriers.
- At the end of the movement, immediately attempt a **Stealth** check to **Hide**, even while combat is ongoing.
- Gain a **+6 bonus** to the Stealth check made as part of Phantom Step.
- If successful, you become **Hidden** and gain the normal benefits of attacking from Hidden.
- **The first attack you make after successfully becoming Hidden through Phantom Step gains a +2 bonus to its attack roll.**
- If you possess the **Camouflage** talent, you may immediately enter **Camouflage** after successfully becoming Hidden, ignoring its normal requirement of being out of combat.

#### Limitations

- You are **not invisible** while using Phantom Step.
- Phantom Step must begin by **leaving a creature's melee reach**.
- You must end the movement in an **unoccupied space**.
- Creatures with magical detection or similar abilities can still detect you normally.

---

### Lore

Only the most accomplished Phantom Rangers ever reach this level of mastery. Their movements become so fluid that enemies often question whether they are pursuing a single hunter or several spectral figures moving through the battlefield. Every disappearance creates uncertainty, and every reappearance reminds their quarry that nowhere is truly safe.

Within the Ranger Lodges, these hunters are entrusted with eliminating the most elusive prey in Asteria. They are taught that the greatest strike is not the strongest, but the one their enemy never saw coming. By mastering both concealment and timing, they transform every battlefield into the perfect hunting ground.

---

> *"A phantom never rushes the hunt. It simply appears where victory is already waiting."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 5
### Description

The Ranger has achieved complete mastery of Phantom Ranger, becoming a living myth among the Ranger Lodges. During battle they appear to exist between the physical world and the Spirit of the Wild, effortlessly slipping through enemy formations before vanishing into the landscape. Every movement is deliberate, every disappearance calculated, and every reappearance marks another step toward the inevitable end of the hunt.

To the Ranger's quarry, combat becomes a nightmare. The hunter never remains in one place long enough to be cornered, striking from impossible angles before fading back into the wilderness. Those who survive rarely agree on what they witnessed—only that the Ranger was never where they expected them to be.

---

### Effects

- **Cost:** 120 MP.
- **Duration:** 5 Minutes.
- **Uses:** 2 uses per **Short Rest**.

While Phantom Ranger is active:

- **Once per turn**, after leaving a creature's melee reach, you may activate **Phantom Step**.
- During **Phantom Step**:
  - Move up to **18 metres**.
  - **Non-magical melee attacks**, including **Opportunity Attacks**, pass harmlessly through your spectral form.
  - **Magical melee attacks, spells, magical ranged attacks, and magical area effects** affect you normally.
  - You may move through creatures of **Huge size or smaller**, but not through walls, solid objects, terrain, or magical barriers.
- At the end of the movement, immediately attempt a **Stealth** check to **Hide**, even while combat is ongoing.
- Gain a **+8 bonus** to the Stealth check made as part of Phantom Step.
- If successful, you become **Hidden** and gain the normal benefits of attacking from Hidden.
- **The first attack you make after successfully becoming Hidden through Phantom Step gains a +4 bonus to its attack roll.**
- If you possess the **Camouflage** talent, you may immediately enter **Camouflage** after successfully becoming Hidden, ignoring its normal requirement of being out of combat.
- If your first attack from Hidden **hits**, you may immediately activate **Phantom Step** again **without consuming your once-per-turn Phantom Step**, provided you still have movement available. This additional Phantom Step cannot trigger another free Phantom Step.

#### Limitations

- You are **not invisible** while using Phantom Step.
- Phantom Step must begin by **leaving a creature's melee reach**.
- You must end each Phantom Step in an **unoccupied space**.
- Creatures with magical detection or similar abilities can still detect you normally.
- The additional Phantom Step may only occur **once per turn**.

---

### Lore

Only a handful of Rangers throughout Asteria's history have ever reached the fifth rank of Phantom Ranger. They are remembered not merely as exceptional hunters, but as legends who seemed to become one with the wilderness itself. Their prey often believed they had escaped, only to discover the Phantom Ranger silently waiting farther along the trail.

Within the Ranger Lodges, these masters are known as the **Ghosts of the Wild**. They embody the Ranger's highest ideal—not overwhelming strength or unmatched speed, but absolute control of the hunt. Every disappearance creates uncertainty, every reappearance creates opportunity, and every strike reminds their quarry that there is no refuge from a hunter who has become part of the wilderness.

---

> *"You cannot pursue a ghost. By the time you find where it stood, it is already deciding where you will fall."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood, First Phantom Ranger**

# Trophy Hunter

## Overview
The greatest Rangers do not simply hunt—they learn from every victory. Each dangerous beast, monstrous predator, and legendary creature defeated becomes another lesson etched into memory. By studying the anatomy, behaviour, and weaknesses of their prey, the Ranger steadily builds an unmatched understanding of the world's most dangerous creatures.

Trophy Hunter marks the beginning of this journey. Rather than collecting trophies for vanity, the Ranger preserves them as reminders of hard-earned knowledge. Every fang, claw, horn, or hide represents another hunt survived and another weakness uncovered. Against creatures they have studied before, the Ranger fights with calm confidence, knowing exactly where to strike and what mistakes to avoid.

---

## Rank 1
### Description

The greatest Rangers do not simply hunt—they learn from every victory. Each dangerous beast, monstrous predator, and legendary creature defeated becomes another lesson etched into memory. By studying the anatomy, behaviour, and weaknesses of their prey, the Ranger steadily builds an unmatched understanding of the world's most dangerous creatures.

Trophy Hunter marks the beginning of this journey. Rather than collecting trophies for vanity, the Ranger preserves them as reminders of hard-earned knowledge. Every fang, claw, horn, or hide represents another hunt survived and another weakness uncovered. Against creatures they have studied before, the Ranger fights with calm confidence, knowing exactly where to strike and what mistakes to avoid.

---

### Effects

- Whenever you personally participate in defeating a **Beast**, **Monster**, or other GM-approved creature, you may spend **1 hour** harvesting a trophy from its remains.
- Record the harvested trophy in a **Trophy Journal**.
- While fighting a creature of a species recorded within your Trophy Journal:
  - Gain a **+2 bonus to attack rolls** against that species.
  - Gain a **+2 bonus to Survival, Nature, and Investigation** checks made to identify, track, or study that species.
- You may only benefit from **one Trophy Hunter bonus** at a time.
- Harvesting a trophy does not prevent normal harvesting of crafting materials.

---

### Lore

Within the Ranger Lodges, every trophy tells a story. Some display the claw of a cave bear that nearly ended their first hunt, while others preserve the fang of a wyvern or the feather of a great roc. These keepsakes are not symbols of pride alone—they are lessons carried into every future hunt.

Veteran Rangers often possess collections spanning decades, each one representing a creature whose secrets they have uncovered. Apprentices are encouraged to study these trophies, for the wisdom gained from a single successful hunt may one day save countless lives.

---

> *"The greatest reward from every hunt is not the trophy—it is the knowledge that ensures the next one ends the same way."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 2
### Description

The Ranger's collection of trophies has grown into a living record of experience. Every hunt adds another lesson, allowing the Ranger to recognise subtle differences between creatures of the same family and predict their behaviour before battle even begins. The knowledge gained through years of hunting becomes just as deadly as any weapon they carry.

As the Trophy Journal expands, the Ranger develops an instinct for identifying vulnerable anatomy, common attack patterns, and survival habits. Against familiar prey, hesitation disappears, replaced by calm confidence earned through countless successful hunts.

---

### Effects

- Whenever you personally participate in defeating a **Beast**, **Monster**, or other GM-approved creature, you may spend **1 hour** harvesting a trophy from its remains.
- Record the harvested trophy within your **Trophy Journal**.
- While fighting a creature belonging to a species or creature family recorded within your Trophy Journal:
  - Gain a **+3 bonus to attack rolls** against that species or family.
  - Gain a **+3 bonus** to **Survival**, **Nature**, and **Investigation** checks made to identify, track, or study that species or family.
  - Gain **Advantage** on checks made to recall information about that species.
- You may only benefit from **one Trophy Hunter bonus** at a time.
- Harvesting a trophy does not prevent normal harvesting of crafting materials.
- The GM may allow closely related creatures to count as the same creature family (for example, Wolves, Dire Wolves, and Elder Wolves).

---

### Lore

Veteran Rangers often say that every scar tells a story, but every trophy tells a lesson. Over time, the Trophy Journal becomes more than a catalogue of victories—it becomes a field guide filled with hard-earned knowledge gathered through countless dangerous encounters.

Within the Ranger Lodges, apprentices are encouraged to study the journals of experienced hunters before undertaking dangerous expeditions. Many legendary beasts have been defeated not through overwhelming strength, but because a Ranger recognised a familiar weakness preserved within the pages of a Trophy Journal.

---

> *"Strength wins a hunt once. Knowledge wins every hunt that follows."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 3
### Description

Years of relentless hunting have transformed the Ranger into a living bestiary. Every creature added to the Trophy Journal deepens their understanding of the natural world, allowing them to recognise strengths, weaknesses, and behaviours with only a brief observation. To the Ranger, no trophy is merely a keepsake—it is another lesson that may save lives during future hunts.

This accumulated knowledge grants the Ranger remarkable insight into familiar prey. By studying trophies and recalling past encounters, they instinctively recognise where to strike, which attacks to avoid, and how best to exploit the creature's natural weaknesses. Against known prey, experience becomes as valuable as skill.

---

### Effects

- Whenever you personally participate in defeating a **Beast**, **Monster**, or other GM-approved creature, you may spend **1 hour** harvesting a trophy from its remains.
- Record the harvested trophy within your **Trophy Journal**.
- While fighting a creature belonging to a species or creature family recorded within your Trophy Journal:
  - Gain a **+4 bonus to attack rolls** against that species or family.
  - Gain a **+4 bonus** to **Survival**, **Nature**, and **Investigation** checks made to identify, track, or study that species or family.
  - Gain **Advantage** on checks made to recall information about that species.
- After successfully identifying a creature recorded in your Trophy Journal, you learn one of the following (GM's choice if unknown):
  - One Resistance.
  - One Immunity.
  - One Vulnerability.
  - One notable combat behaviour or special ability.
- You may only benefit from **one Trophy Hunter bonus** at a time.
- Harvesting a trophy does not prevent normal harvesting of crafting materials.

---

### Lore

Senior Rangers often spend as much time studying their Trophy Journals as they do hunting. Every page records another hard-earned lesson, allowing future encounters to begin with knowledge instead of uncertainty. To outsiders the collection appears to be a display of impressive trophies; to a Ranger it is a lifetime of experience preserved for the next hunt.

Within the Ranger Lodges, journals belonging to legendary hunters are treasured relics. Entire generations of Rangers have survived impossible encounters simply because a forgotten note revealed a creature's weakness before the battle began.

---

> *"Every beast carries a weakness. A Trophy Hunter simply learns to remember them all."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 4
### Description

The Ranger's Trophy Journal has become one of the finest collections of hunting knowledge in Asteria. Years of studying monsters, beasts, and legendary creatures have taught the Ranger that every family of creatures shares common instincts, weaknesses, and methods of survival. What was once knowledge of individual species now extends to entire bloodlines.

Rather than relying on memory alone, the Ranger instinctively recognises subtle traits shared between related creatures. A dragon's stance, a wolf's hunting pattern, or the posture of an undead guardian immediately reveals valuable information gathered from countless previous hunts. Against familiar creature families, the Ranger rarely enters battle unprepared.

---

### Effects

- Whenever you personally participate in defeating a **Beast**, **Monster**, or other GM-approved creature, you may spend **1 hour** harvesting a trophy from its remains.
- Record the harvested trophy within your **Trophy Journal**.
- While fighting a creature belonging to a **recorded creature family**, gain:
  - **+5 bonus to attack rolls**.
  - **+5 bonus** to **Survival**, **Nature**, and **Investigation** checks made to identify, track, or study that creature family.
  - **Advantage** on checks made to recall information about that creature family.
- After successfully identifying a creature recorded in your Trophy Journal, immediately learn **two** of the following:
  - One Resistance.
  - One Immunity.
  - One Vulnerability.
  - One notable combat behaviour or special ability.
- Once per encounter, you may reroll a failed **Nature**, **Survival**, or **Investigation** check made against a recorded creature family. You must use the new result.
- You may only benefit from **one Trophy Hunter bonus** at a time.
- Harvesting trophies does not prevent normal harvesting of crafting materials.

---

### Lore

Master Trophy Hunters are no longer recognised by the number of trophies they possess, but by the knowledge they carry into every hunt. Entire creature families become familiar to them, allowing even newly encountered variants to be understood through years of accumulated experience. Few creatures can truly surprise a Ranger who has spent decades studying the natural world.

Within the Ranger Lodges, the journals of these hunters are considered priceless archives. Generations of Rangers continue to add new discoveries, ensuring that every successful hunt strengthens those who will one day follow the same path.

---

> *"Every creature leaves behind more than a trophy. It leaves behind the wisdom to defeat the next one."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 5
### Description

The Ranger has become one of Asteria's greatest Trophy Hunters, possessing a Trophy Journal that spans a lifetime of legendary hunts. Every beast, monster, and apex predator defeated has left behind more than a physical trophy—it has contributed to an unparalleled understanding of the natural world. No hunt is wasted, and every encounter strengthens the Ranger's mastery over future prey.

The Trophy Journal is now considered a priceless archive, containing knowledge that cannot be found in books or taught through study alone. When facing a familiar creature, the Ranger instinctively recognises its strengths, weaknesses, behaviours, and patterns of attack before battle has truly begun. To many, it appears almost supernatural, yet it is simply the reward of surviving countless impossible hunts.

---

### Effects

- Whenever you personally participate in defeating a **Beast**, **Monster**, or other GM-approved creature, you may spend **1 hour** harvesting a trophy from its remains.
- Record the harvested trophy within your **Trophy Journal**.
- While fighting a creature belonging to a **recorded creature family**, gain:
  - **+6 bonus to attack rolls**.
  - **+6 bonus** to **Survival**, **Nature**, and **Investigation** checks made to identify, track, or study that creature family.
  - **Advantage** on checks made to recall information about that creature family.
- Immediately learn **all known**:
  - Resistances.
  - Immunities.
  - Vulnerabilities.
  - Combat behaviours.
  - Special abilities.
  - Natural weaknesses.
- Once per encounter, you may reroll a failed **Attack Roll**, **Nature**, **Survival**, or **Investigation** check made against a recorded creature family. You must use the new result.
- You may only benefit from **one Trophy Hunter bonus** at a time.
- Harvesting trophies does not prevent normal harvesting of crafting materials.

---

### Lore

Only a handful of Rangers throughout history have ever completed a Trophy Journal worthy of legend. These individuals are sought by kingdoms, guilds, and scholars alike, for their knowledge of the world's most dangerous creatures surpasses that of nearly every library in existence. Their journals become treasured relics, copied and preserved so future generations may continue the endless pursuit of understanding the wilderness.

Among the Ranger Lodges, these masters are known simply as **Trophy Hunters**—a title that carries immense respect. They do not hunt for glory or recognition, but because every creature overcome adds another page to the ever-growing story of the wild. Their greatest weapon is no longer their bow or blade, but the wisdom earned through every hunt they have survived.

---

> *"The greatest trophy is not the fang upon your wall—it is the knowledge that ensures no creature defeats you twice."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood, First Trophy Hunter**

# Volley

## Overview
The Ranger channels primal magic into a single arrow before firing it high into the heavens. As the arrow reaches its peak, it bursts into countless spectral copies that descend upon the battlefield in an unrelenting rain of magical arrows. Rather than striking a single target, Volley transforms the chosen area into a deadly storm where every heartbeat brings the threat of another falling arrow.

At its earliest stage, the Ranger has only limited control over this magical barrage. Once unleashed, the spectral arrows cannot distinguish friend from foe, forcing allies and enemies alike to seek shelter or risk being caught beneath the storm. Though dangerous to everyone within its reach, a well-placed Volley can completely reshape the battlefield and halt an advancing force.

---

## Rank 1
### Description

The Ranger channels primal magic into a single arrow before firing it high into the heavens. As the arrow reaches its peak, it bursts into countless spectral copies that descend upon the battlefield in an unrelenting rain of magical arrows. Rather than striking a single target, Volley transforms the chosen area into a deadly storm where every heartbeat brings the threat of another falling arrow.

At its earliest stage, the Ranger has only limited control over this magical barrage. Once unleashed, the spectral arrows cannot distinguish friend from foe, forcing allies and enemies alike to seek shelter or risk being caught beneath the storm. Though dangerous to everyone within its reach, a well-placed Volley can completely reshape the battlefield and halt an advancing force.

---

### Effects

- **Cost:** 120 MP.
- **Uses:** 2 uses per **Long Rest**.
- Choose a point you can see within **60 metres**.
- Spectral arrows rain down in a **10-metre radius** centred on the chosen point.
- The volley remains active **until the start of the second Initiative Order after your own**.
- A creature must make a **DC 13 Agility (Dodge) Check**:
  - The first time it enters the affected area on its turn.
  - Or when it starts its turn within the affected area.
- A creature can only be affected **once** by each use of Volley.
- On a failed check, the creature takes **6d8 Magical Piercing Damage**.
- On a successful check, the creature takes **half damage**.
- **All creatures**, including allies, are affected by Volley.
- Volley requires a **clear path to the sky** and cannot be used underground, beneath a solid roof, or inside enclosed structures unless the GM determines there is sufficient overhead clearance.
- The spectral arrows disappear immediately after striking and cannot be recovered.

---

### Lore

Volley is considered one of the Ranger Lodges' oldest battlefield techniques, created for the rare occasions when a single arrow was not enough to turn the tide of battle. By surrendering precision for overwhelming area control, the Ranger commands the wilderness itself to answer their call, transforming one arrow into a storm capable of scattering entire warbands.

The earliest practitioners quickly learned that such power demanded restraint. Until complete mastery is achieved, the magical arrows recognise no friend or foe, making careful positioning as important as the technique itself. Veteran Rangers often warn apprentices that a poorly placed Volley can be just as dangerous to allies as it is to their enemies.

---

> *"One arrow begins the hunt. A thousand arrows decide its end."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

The Ranger's mastery over Volley continues to grow, allowing them to sustain a larger and more devastating rain of spectral arrows. What was once an uncontrollable barrage now falls with greater precision, covering a wider portion of the battlefield while maintaining its relentless assault. Though allies are still at risk, an experienced Ranger learns to position the storm where it will inflict the greatest harm upon their enemies.

As the enchanted arrow bursts overhead, countless shimmering copies spiral downward in waves, forcing creatures to either abandon their ground or endure the unending rain of magical projectiles. Few formations can remain intact beneath such overwhelming pressure.

---

- **Uses:** 2 uses per **Long Rest**.

- Spectral arrows rain down in a **15-metre radius** centred on the chosen point.
- The volley remains active **until the start of the second Initiative Order after your own**.

  - Or when it starts its turn within the affected area.

---

Those who survive a Rank II Volley often describe it as standing beneath a violent storm rather than an attack. The sky darkens with spectral arrows, each one guided by primal magic instead of a Ranger's hand. Escape becomes the only sensible option, as remaining beneath the barrage invites certain injury.

Within the Ranger Lodges, apprentices are taught that Volley is as much a tool of battlefield control as it is a weapon. A well-placed barrage can scatter enemy formations, deny strategic ground, and force even the most disciplined warriors to abandon their positions.

> *"A hunter does not always need to strike the prey. Sometimes, they simply decide where the prey is allowed to stand."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 3

The Ranger's command over primal magic has matured into a truly devastating battlefield technique. Every volley is guided by the will of the wilderness, transforming open ground into a deadly killing field.

Although the Ranger's control has improved considerably, the magical storm still shows no favour. Friend and foe alike must respect its destructive power, making careful positioning and battlefield awareness essential to those fighting alongside the Ranger.

---

- On a failed check, the creature takes **8d8 Magical Piercing Damage**.
- On a successful check, the creature takes **half damage**.
- **All creatures**, including allies, are affected by Volley.
- Volley requires a **clear path to the sky** and cannot be used underground, beneath a solid roof, or inside enclosed structures unless the GM determines there is sufficient overhead clearance.
- The spectral arrows disappear immediately after striking and cannot be recovered.

---

### Lore

Only experienced Rangers are entrusted with the third rank of Volley. By this stage, the technique is no longer viewed as merely a powerful attack but as a method of controlling the battlefield itself. Entire companies have been forced to abandon defensive positions as waves of shimmering arrows descended from above, leaving no safe place to stand.

Veteran Huntmasters teach that Volley is not intended to eliminate every foe outright. Its true strength lies in forcing the enemy to move exactly where the Ranger wants them to go, allowing allies to exploit the chaos while the storm rages overhead.

---

> *"The wisest prey does not fear the arrow. It fears the ground the hunter has chosen."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 4
### Description

The Ranger's mastery over Volley has reached a level where the primal magic responds to their intent as much as their aim. The storm of spectral arrows no longer falls as an indiscriminate barrage, but as a controlled rain directed toward those the Ranger wishes to punish. Entire battlefields can be reshaped as allies advance beneath a sky that only their enemies need fear.

The arrow still ascends into the heavens before splitting into countless magical copies, but the Ranger now instinctively guides the storm's path through primal will. Enemies find themselves trapped beneath a relentless downpour while companions move unhindered through the chaos, allowing coordinated assaults that were once impossible.

---

### Effects

- **Cost:** 180 MP.
- **Uses:** 2 uses per **Long Rest**.
- Choose a point you can see within **105 metres**.
- Spectral arrows rain down in a **20-metre radius** centred on the chosen point.
- The volley remains active **until the start of the second Initiative Order after your own**.
- When activating Volley, you may designate **up to 5 allied creatures** that are **immune** to this ability's effects.

  - The first time it enters the affected area on its turn.
  - Or when it starts its turn within the affected area.
- A creature can only be affected **once** by each use of Volley.
- On a failed check, the creature takes **9d8 Magical Piercing Damage**.
- On a successful check, the creature takes **half damage**.

- Volley requires a **clear path to the sky** and cannot be used underground, beneath a solid roof, or inside enclosed structures unless the GM determines there is sufficient overhead clearance.
- The spectral arrows disappear immediately after striking and cannot be recovered.

---

### Lore

Few Rangers ever develop enough control to command Volley without endangering their companions. Those who do are regarded as battlefield tacticians as much as hunters, capable of directing a magical storm with remarkable precision while their allies advance unharmed beneath it.

Within the Ranger Lodges, this achievement marks the transition from master hunter to battlefield commander. Entire warbands have marched confidently through a storm of spectral arrows, trusting completely in the judgement of the Ranger who called it forth. To witness such mastery is to understand that the wilderness itself now fights beside them.

---

> *"A storm without control is destruction. A storm guided by a Ranger is victory."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 5
### Description

The Ranger has perfected one of the Ranger Lodges' most feared techniques. A single enchanted arrow is loosed into the heavens where it bursts into an immense storm of primal energy, creating an unrelenting rain of spectral arrows across the battlefield. Every arrow is guided by the Ranger's will, striking only those they deem worthy of the hunt.

No longer an indiscriminate barrage, the final form of Volley demonstrates complete mastery over both archery and primal magic. Allies advance unhindered beneath the storm while enemies desperately seek shelter from a relentless rain that seems to pursue every movement. Entire battlefields can be dominated with a single shot, allowing the Ranger to dictate the flow of combat from incredible distances.

Among the Ranger Lodges, only the greatest Huntmasters are entrusted with this technique. To witness a master unleash Volley is to watch the sky itself become the Ranger's greatest weapon.

---

### Effects

- **Cost:** 200 MP.
- **Uses:** 2 uses per **Long Rest**.
- Choose a point you can see within **120 metres**.
- Spectral arrows rain down in a **25-metre radius** centred on the chosen point.
- The volley remains active **until the start of the second Initiative Order after your own**.
- When activating Volley, you may designate **any number of allied creatures** that are **immune** to this ability's effects.
- A creature must make a **DC 21 Agility (Dodge) Check**:
  - The first time it enters the affected area on its turn.
  - Or when it starts its turn within the affected area.
- A creature can only be affected **once** by each use of Volley.
- On a failed check, the creature takes **10d8 Magical Piercing Damage**.
- On a successful check, the creature takes **half damage**.
- Creatures that fail the Dodge Check have their **Movement Speed reduced by half until the end of their next turn** as spectral arrows pin them down and disrupt their advance.
- Volley requires a **clear path to the sky** and cannot be used underground, beneath a solid roof, or inside enclosed structures unless the GM determines there is sufficient overhead clearance.
- The spectral arrows disappear immediately after striking and cannot be recovered.

---

### Lore

The fifth rank of Volley is considered the pinnacle of battlefield archery. Few Rangers throughout history have possessed the discipline, magical control, and experience required to command such a devastating storm without endangering those fighting beside them. Those who achieve this mastery are remembered not only as legendary hunters, but as protectors capable of turning impossible battles into decisive victories.

Stories tell of entire armies brought to a halt beneath a sky filled with spectral arrows while allied forces advanced untouched through the storm. To the Ranger Lodges, this technique is the ultimate expression of the hunter's creed—not simply to defeat the prey, but to control the battlefield so completely that escape becomes impossible.

---

> *"When the heavens answer the hunter's call, even armies learn there is nowhere left to run."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood, First Huntmaster of the Emerald Lodge**
